 Judgment
Heard Sri.N.R.Kuppelur, Sri.Suresh Shettammanavar and Sri.Suresh S. Gundi learned counsel for the parties.

2. Insurance company of the lorry bearing No.KA-36 A/2976 is in appeal challenging the apportionment of the compensation awarded in MVC No.219/2017 dated 25.08.2019 attributing the negligence on the part of the driver of the said lorry.

3. Facts in brief which are utmost necessary for disposal of the appeal are as under:
3.1 Claimant is one Sri.Vijaya kumar who is brother of Chandappa S/o Sangappa Chalawadi who lost his life in road traffic accident.
Said Chandappa was working as cleaner in lorry bearing No.KA-36/A-2976. 3.2

On 19.04.2013 at about 4.10 a.m.
when the Chandappa was proceeding in the said lorry as a cleaner from Lingasugar to Belagavi on Raichur-Belagavi road, NC: 2024:KHC-D:3655 there was a lorry which has been parked without proper indication near Halakki cross of Muragod village of Saundatti taluk.
Not noticing the parked lorry, driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-36A/2976 dashed against the parked lorry bearing No.OR 16-B/3161.
On account of the said accident, Chandappa sustained grievous injuries and lost his life.

3.3 Claim petition on contest came to be allowed in a sum of Rs.12,62,600/- and apportioned the quantum of compensation to be paid by the offending lorry at 90%
and 10% on the insurance company of the parked lorry.
4. Being aggrieved by the same, insurance company of lorry bearing No.KA-36/A-2976 is in appeal.

5. Sri.N.R.Kuppelur reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum contended that lorry was parked on the road without sufficient indication and therefore at least 50% of contributory negligence is to be attributed to both the lorries and sought for allowing the appeal.
He also contended that the quantum of compensation is on the higher side so also rate of interest.
7. Per contra, Sri.S.S.Gundi and Sri.Suresh Shettammanavar supported the impugned judgment.

sentences.text: Having heard the parties, this court has perused the material on record meticulously.

9. On such perusal of the material on record, it is crystal clear that the accident has occurred on account of the negligent driving of the lorry bearing No.KA-36A/2976 in not expecting the unexpected and also on account of the negligent parking of the lorry on the highway.
10. Therefore, there is sufficient force in the argument canvassed on behalf of the appellant that the negligence should be apportioned between the parked lorry and the offending lorry.

11. In a matter of this nature, attributing 50% of the negligence to drivers of both the lorry would meet the ends of justice, having regard to the specific regulation NC: 2024:KHC-D:3655 that no lorry can be parked on highway that too without indication.

12. Insofar as quantum of compensation is concerned, tribunal has taken into consideration the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- whereas in the absence of proper proof of income, amount payable for the accidental death of 2013 is that of Rs.7,000/-.
Since the deceased was working as a cleaner, he cannot be equated that of a person without any income.
Therefore, taking income at Rs.8,000/- p.m. is just and proper.
Accordingly, there is hardly any scope for reduction of the compensation.
13. Taking note of the interest rate payable on the fixed deposit by the banks at relevant point of time awarding of interest at 7% is just and proper.

14. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.

NC: 2024:KHC-D:3655 ii) While maintaining the quantum of compensation and the interest rate there on, adjudged compensation is to be paid by the appellant and -insurance company of parked lorry bearing No. OR 16-B/3161 is to be apportioned in the ratio of 50% each.
iii) Amount in deposit is transmitted to the tribunal.
iv) Balance amount is to be deposited by both the insurance company as per the modified award within four weeks.
v) Excess amount if any deposited by the appellant is ordered to be returned to the appellant under due identification.
